Build terms rows for a functional or Cockerham (a, d) pair

Source: R/genome_effect_terms_builders.R
ad_terms.Rd

Turns each locus's additive and dominance coefficients into the terms rows define_genome_effect_terms() writes: one row per non-zero coefficient. Functional coding gives an additive row centred at 0.5 and an indicator row on the heterozygote; Cockerham coding gives additive and dominance rows centred at p.

  • coding = "functional" (default): the genotypic value is a * (g - 1) + d * 1[g = 1], where g is the dosage of allele 1 (0, 1 or 2). So a is half the difference between the two homozygotes and d the heterozygote's deviation from their midpoint. Values are absolute, so the genetic values have a non-zero mean.

  • coding = "cockerham": a is the average effect alpha and d the dominance effect on the HWE dominance contrast, which is -2p^2, 2pq, -2q^2 at dosages 0, 1, 2. Values are deviations with mean 0 under HWE at p.

Usage

ad_terms(
  locus_name,
  a,
  d = 0,
  p,
  coding = c("functional", "cockerham"),
  effect_name = NULL,
  report = TRUE
)

Arguments

locus_name

Character vector of distinct locus names (from genome_meta).

a

Numeric additive coefficient(s), one per locus or one recycled.

d

Numeric dominance coefficient(s), one per locus or one recycled. Default 0 (no dominance row).

p

Allele-1 frequency per locus, in [0, 1], one per locus or one recycled. Always required: the centre under Cockerham coding, and the basis of the reported mean under functional coding (where it does not change the stored rows). Use the frequency of the population the model describes, e.g. from extract_allele_freq().

coding

"functional" (default) or "cockerham"; see Description.

effect_name

Optional label carried onto every row.

report

Logical; print the implied genetic mean as a message. Default TRUE.

Value

A terms data frame with the fixed builder column set (see aa_terms()): one row per non-zero coefficient. term_id encodes the builder, the locus and a / d, so it never collides with another builder's ids when outputs are rbind()-ed.

The reported mean is not written anywhere

For functional coding the implied mean of the genetic component is mu = a(p - q) + 2pq*d. It is reported and stored nowhere — in particular not in phenotype_meta.mean, which would double-count it once non-additive genetic values reach the phenotype layer, because the raw genetic values already have expectation mu. The running total across loci is reported only because every term here is a single-locus main effect; no such total exists for an epistatic term, whose expectation depends on joint genotype frequencies and LD.

See also

define_genome_effect_terms(), aa_terms(), genotype_terms().

Examples

# The rows only; nothing is written
ad_terms(c("Locus_10", "Locus_20"), a = c(0.4, -0.2), d = c(0.1, 0),
         p = c(0.3, 0.5))
#> Implied genetic mean (functional coding), reported only — written to no table: Locus_10 mu = -0.118; Locus_20 mu =  0.000. Running total over these single-locus main effects: -0.118.
#>           term_id locus_name contrast_name center_value copy_count_value
#> 1 ad:8:Locus_10#a   Locus_10      additive          0.5               NA
#> 2 ad:8:Locus_20#a   Locus_20      additive          0.5               NA
#> 3 ad:8:Locus_10#d   Locus_10     indicator           NA                2
#>   dosage_value genome_value effect_name
#> 1           NA          0.4        <NA>
#> 2           NA         -0.2        <NA>
#> 3            1          0.1        <NA>

# The same model's statistical (Cockerham) coefficients at p = 0.3
# (Locus_10 only): alpha = a + (q - p) d
ad_terms("Locus_10", a = 0.4 + (0.7 - 0.3) * 0.1, d = 0.1, p = 0.3,
         coding = "cockerham")
#> Implied genetic mean (cockerham coding), reported only — written to no table: Locus_10 mu = 0. Running total over these single-locus main effects: 0.
#>           term_id locus_name contrast_name center_value copy_count_value
#> 1 ad:8:Locus_10#a   Locus_10      additive          0.3               NA
#> 2 ad:8:Locus_10#d   Locus_10     dominance          0.3               NA
#>   dosage_value genome_value effect_name
#> 1           NA         0.44        <NA>
#> 2           NA         0.10        <NA>

# Write them for a trait
set.seed(1)
pop <- open_pop(pop_name = "ad_example", db_name = ":memory:") |>
  define_genome(n_loci = 60, n_chr = 2, chr_len_Mb = 100) |>
  define_founder_haplotypes(n_haplotypes = 100)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpK5kjor/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Opened in-memory population 'ad_example'
#> Defined genome: 60 loci across 2 chromosomes | chr lengths (Mb): all equal to 100 Mb
#>   Tables written: genome_meta, genome_map, ind_haplotype, ind_genotype, ind_crossover, chr_inheritance, chr_recombination, genome_effects, genome_effect_members, genome_effect_member_origins
#>   Views created: genome_effect_terms, genome_effect_loci
#> Generating 100 founder haplotypes (method = "uniform")...
#>   Created founder_haplotypes (100 haplotypes x 60 loci)
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("founder_haplotypes") |>
  add_founders(n_males = 10, n_females = 10, line_name = "A")
#> Added 20 founders (10 males, 10 females) to line 'A'
pop <- define_trait(pop, "ADG")
#> Added trait 'ADG'.
pop <- pop |>
  define_genome_effect_terms("ADG",
    ad_terms("Locus_10", a = 0.4, d = 0.1, p = 0.3),
    effect_owner = "qtl_map")
#> Implied genetic mean (functional coding), reported only — written to no table: Locus_10 mu = -0.118. Running total over these single-locus main effects: -0.118.
#> Wrote 2 genome-effect terms (2 member rows) for trait 'ADG' under owner 'qtl_map' [append].
close_pop(pop)
